title: Kernel closure for integral constructible internal modules
statement: Let ℓ be prime, E a finite normed extension of ℚ_ℓ, and X a scheme with noetherian underlying space. For the continuous integral coefficient ring of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], kernels of morphisms between internal modules which are constructible by stratified local finite presentations are again constructible.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1), integral finite model comparison

proof.text: Use the one-pivot cover of integralMatrix_pivot_cover. Strong induction on the number of source generators proves local finite presentation of the kernel of a finite free matrix with locally free rational cokernel. The zero branch uses the free source. In the pivot branch the categorical pivotKernelIso identifies the kernel with the kernel of d-r*c, with strictly fewer source generators. The proved pivotCokernelIso and mappedPivotCokernelIso identify the rational cokernel with that of d-r*c because the rational pivot is invertible. The proved rationalCokernelFree_pullback transports local freeness through the covering and coefficient comparison. Thus the induction hypothesis applies. No full Smith form or finite integral module classification is needed.

For a finite free cokernel presentation descended from a locally finitely presented module P on the noetherian base, use the proved lfp_extend helper to extend P to E. Apply exists_finiteFree_cover_of_condensedField_lfp, lifting E to ULift E for the scheme universe and transporting by liftCoefficientIso. Pull that free cover through both presentation covers. The proved scalar-extension/pullback comparison and extendScalarsComapSquareIso transport its local freeness to the actual coefficient ring on the covering scheme. Apply the matrix-kernel induction and transport back.

Generic cokernel closure makes coker f locally finitely presented. On a common finite-presentation cover, choose presentations M=coker a and N=coker b. The existing freeEpiLocalSplitting lifts the source generators through the free presentation of N on a further covering, giving t and the augmented map delta=(b,t) which presents coker f. The preceding descended-matrix assertion gives locally finitely presented kernels of b and delta. The fully proved kernelCokernelCompIso identifies the cokernel of their natural map with ker(pi_M followed by f). The fully proved kernelDescCokernelIso then identifies the cokernel of the source relation map into this module with ker f. Apply generic lfp_cokernel twice and glue the presentation covers.

Use the existing common_lfp_stratification helper from CondensedConstructibleSerre to refine the source and target stratifications. An immersion is a topological embedding, so every stratum has noetherian underlying space. Apply the locally finitely presented kernel result on each stratum, use exact inverse image and the coefficient comap equivalence to identify it with the restricted kernel, and transport the canonical kernel to an arbitrary kernel cone.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.8, Lemma 6.8.7 and Proposition 6.8.11(1), one-pivot reduction and augmented presentations
proof_origin.note: H2: the original kernel-closure hole is reduced by a complete Lean proof to one local integral pivot chart. Strong induction, rational cokernel preservation under a pivot, scalar/pullback comparisons, the two exact cokernel calculations and constructible gluing are all proved. The remaining chart does not assert kernel finiteness or constructibility. Full finite-integral-model invariance and Smith diagonalization are pruned.
